milestones.title: Original browser execution
milestones.foundation: Published local-ISO browser build with the full SDK, software rendering, input, audio and save adapters; working Windows reference reported by the user. Browser gameplay remains unverified.
milestones.goal: Play one original minigame through its original menus, round and results entirely in a desktop browser.

criteria.text: Complete original menu → minigame → results → menu three consecutive times, with original-program graphics and audible audio responding to recorded player input, and no unsupported stop or fault.
Execute the game entirely in the browser using compatible player-local content. A privately prepared local module may support this developer gate; end-user browser conversion is required by M2.

Retain source/build/module identities, browser/device details and the input/capture record, with the runtime control/experiment comparison and independent audit. The prototype and standalone component fixtures do not satisfy this gate.

tasks.title: Integrate the original browser round path
tasks.scope: Connect the reached CPU, kernel, graphics, audio and controller requirements through one original round, preserving admission and content guards.

criteria.text: The original title reaches a controllable menu and the selected minigame without replacement rules or scenes.
Reached unsupported behavior stops explicitly; changed CPU/memory/ABI/GPU contracts have targeted checks and independent review.

brief.context: Published local-ISO browser build with the full SDK, software rendering, input, audio and save adapters; working Windows reference reported by the user. Browser gameplay remains unverified. Preserve M44 as the separate accepted startup reference; build on the merged SDK candidate from PR #102.
brief.firstStep: Run the published browser candidate with the compatible player-local ISO. Fix the first actual execution or performance blocker, then reach a controllable original menu and one complete minigame. Reuse the working native reference and existing adapters; do not restart integration. Defer detailed test suites until the browser baseline works.
prerequisites: Inspect current status, task ownership, matching input/source/toolchain identities and any retained native/browser runs. Keep upstream-reported results, local desktop observations, experimental browser results and accepted M44 evidence distinct.

Original-code claims and title execution require the purpose-specific local baseline, retained provenance and focused independent review. Source-owned interface work can proceed without those private inputs.

Keep M44 unchanged. Give the separate SDK candidate explicit resource/import/export/dispatch limits and retain basic bounds, identity and private-content checks. Detailed contract certification and independent correctness review follow the working baseline, before accepted-checkpoint promotion.

deliverables.title: Sustained execution and a viable admission route (MB04–07)
deliverables.doneWhen: Continuing guest execution preserves context and supports responsive browser delivery under a reviewed capacity route; only scenario-required callbacks, waits and timing are implemented.
deliverables.firstStep: Run the published browser candidate with the compatible player-local ISO. Fix the first actual execution or performance blocker, then reach a controllable original menu and one complete minigame. Reuse the working native reference and existing adapters; do not restart integration. Defer detailed test suites until the browser baseline works.

deliverables.title: Original graphics and the first title frame (MB11–17)
deliverables.doneWhen: The existing software-renderer path presents an identified original frame with correct required textures, shaders and draw state. Fix observed fidelity or performance gaps; add acceleration only when measurements justify it.

deliverables.title: Original sound processing and audible output (MB18–19)
deliverables.doneWhen: Required original sound-buffer/voice behavior reaches one browser output route with sample, timing, activation and lifetime evidence.

deliverables.title: Selected startup and original resource lifecycle (MB02–03, MB08–10)
deliverables.doneWhen: The selected path consumes actual player-local resource bytes with checked buffers, statuses, ownership and cleanup. Pull the exact needed read or continuation ahead of its dependent graphics/audio proof.

deliverables.title: Owned input, original menu and one complete round (MB20–23)
deliverables.doneWhen: One chosen host input method reaches original pad polling; the original menu selects the target, a round reaches results, and execution returns to the menu without replacement rules or scenes.

validation: Before the working baseline, compile and run the actual affected path, inspect its output/failure and use only quick diagnostic checks. Batch shared-interface fixes and reuse passing evidence. Detailed testing, broad matrices and repeated per-caller/historical audits come later.
After the baseline works, complete correctness/fidelity/regression testing and independent CPU/memory/ABI/GPU review before promoting accepted evidence or closing the applicable acceptance criteria.
Keep a brief record of what ran, observed output/failure, source/module/input identities, next fix and elapsed effort. Preserve raw private logs locally; expand formal evidence after the baseline.
outOfScope: Full catalog/parity and end-user browser-local conversion belong to M2.
Online play, accounts/social, broad device matrices and optional polish belong to later milestones.
A fixture, preview, compiler success or counter increase does not close an original browser connection or accept M1.
brief.stopCondition: Continue building and fixing the actual browser path. Missing private game inputs block execution only; report the exact failure and continue independent source work. Preserve M44, content locality and bounds checks. A build or frame alone does not close the browser milestone.

references.purpose: Detailed MB connections, sizes, required features and largest-first order.
Bounded execution, graphics, resource, capacity and audio assignments.
Accepted evidence, separately identified local candidates and current runtime boundary.
Private preflight purpose, targeted checks and measured work records.
SDK-first implementation policy, bounded desktop reference and baseline-first build-run-fix workflow.

tasks.title: Verify original browser gameplay and evidence
tasks.scope: Execute and review the repeatable original-menu/round/results scenario on the identified build.

criteria.text: Record three consecutive original rounds with visible output, audible audio and input-driven state changes.
Bind the reports, independent audit, source/module identities and browser/device environment; list all remaining limits.

brief.context: The three-cycle gate and comparison/audit tools exist, but no accepted original menu/game/results/menu cycle is recorded. Evidence preparation can proceed before the playable candidate; execution and acceptance require that candidate.
brief.firstStep: With the runtime owner, freeze one compatible original build, desktop browser/device, selected minigame, input method and seat recipe. Draft the exact input/capture procedure and identity checklist before scheduling the first end-to-end run.
prerequisites: Use the original playable candidate delivered by m1-build for cycle execution; component fixtures and the independent prototype do not substitute.
Confirm matching local source/module/input identities and purpose-specific replay checks; keep all original-containing captures and raw evidence local.
Agree the control comparison, capture boundaries and independent reviewer before the acceptance run.

deliverables.title: Repeatable selected scenario and capture recipe (MB01, MB24)
deliverables.doneWhen: The exact build, browser/device, minigame, seat/input configuration and menu/round/results/return input recipe are recorded and reproducible.

deliverables.title: Bound candidate identities and retained comparisons
deliverables.doneWhen: Source/build/module/input identities, required retained cases and audit/report bindings agree for the tested candidate; rejected attempts and scope limits remain identified.

deliverables.title: Three consecutive original audiovisual/input cycles
deliverables.doneWhen: Actual original menu/game/results/menu runs complete three times in succession with visible original output, audible original sound, recorded input response and no unsupported stop or fault.

deliverables.title: Independent acceptance review and remaining-limit record
deliverables.doneWhen: The reviewer can reproduce the scenario and assess controls, evidence provenance and required checks. Publish curated outcomes and keep unresolved required capabilities open; an explicit parent acceptance record is still required.

validation: Verify original-program graphics/audio/input through the full scenario rather than combining unrelated component successes.
Retain source/module/browser/device identities, control/experiment comparison and independent audit for the same candidate.
Reproduce any failure with exact conditions and return the gap to its owning MB row before another acceptance attempt.
outOfScope: Completing this child issue does not automatically close or accept its M1 parent.
The gate covers one original minigame on one desktop configuration; complete catalog, end-user conversion and broader devices remain later work.
Do not upload original media, generated title code, original-containing memory/save states or raw private reports.
brief.stopCondition: Stop acceptance on any missing identity, failed invariant, approximate scene/rule substitution, unsupported stop, audiovisual/input mismatch or incomplete cycle. Preserve evidence and report the concrete owning MB gap.

references.purpose: Exact M1 criteria and independent acceptance requirements.
MB01 scenario and MB24 acceptance, with owning connections for failures.
Existing bounded report comparison infrastructure; it does not itself prove a full round.
Purpose-specific retained-input gates and evidence/timing handoff.

milestones.title: Complete local game and conversion
milestones.foundation: Compatible-ISO validation, lazy local disc mounting and browser-save adapters are implemented. Complete browser conversion, catalog coverage and save recovery remain unverified.
milestones.goal: A fresh browser converts the supported player-supplied image and runs the complete original offline game.

criteria.text: From a fresh browser, select the supported image, validate/convert locally and start the original game without a developer toolchain. Exercise unsupported/corrupt input, cancel, clear/reimport and denied/evicted storage; original content never uploads.

Complete the verified catalog/variant/character/arena inventory and original practice, Minigame Frenzy and Tournament flows, with one to four local seats and original CPU behavior. Each required entry passes matching-build reference scenarios; unknown or untested entries remain blockers.

Verify original scoring/ties, rules, timing, movement/collisions, AI, camera/animation/audio and round/tournament progression, plus save/reload after closing and reopening the browser. Retain the full parity matrix and discrepancy record.

tasks.title: Finish browser-local conversion and save recovery
tasks.scope: Connect a compatible player-supplied image to browser-local preparation, original execution and durable local save/reimport handling.

criteria.text: The fresh-browser select → validate → convert → play path works without native helpers or uploaded content.
Unsupported inputs, cancellation, storage denial/eviction, clear/reimport and fresh-session save/reload have observed outcomes.

brief.context: Compatible-ISO validation, lazy local disc mounting and browser-save adapters are implemented. Complete browser conversion, catalog coverage and save recovery remain unverified. Extend the existing SDK browser path; do not replace it with the research preview. Keep all player content and saves local.
brief.firstStep: Run the existing local-ISO intake in a fresh browser profile, identify the first missing import/storage behavior, and implement that gap. A local HTTP host serves application files only; no server conversion or game-content upload.
prerequisites: M1 original browser execution is accepted for the compatible build and runtime route.
Supported image/build identity and conversion limits are documented from retained evidence.
The browser-local content policy and safe unsupported-input behavior remain in force.

deliverables.title: Connect local image selection through validation and conversion
deliverables.doneWhen: A fresh browser can select a supported player-provided image, validate the declared build, run the bounded local conversion path, and launch the accepted original browser runtime without a developer toolchain or a content upload; unsupported and corrupt inputs fail with a visible, recoverable outcome.

deliverables.title: Make cancellation, clear, and reimport lifecycle explicit
deliverables.doneWhen: Cancel, clear local content, and reimport have observed outcomes; cancellation releases active workers/resources, clear removes the selected local data under the documented policy, and a subsequent import starts from a clean session.

deliverables.title: Persist and recover browser-local prepared content safely
deliverables.doneWhen: The chosen browser-local storage path handles denied, quota-failed, and evicted data with actionable status and reimport; it avoids whole-disc buffering beyond the documented limits and never sends original content or derived assets to a server or peer.

deliverables.title: Connect original save persistence and fresh-session reload
deliverables.doneWhen: The accepted original save format and lifecycle are exercised through save, close/reopen, reload, and recovery cases; saved original-containing state remains local and malformed or unavailable saves produce a safe observable result.

deliverables.title: Record conversion and storage boundaries in the UI and docs
deliverables.doneWhen: Supported image/build limits, conversion progress, cancellation, storage failure, clear/reimport, and save recovery behavior are described consistently with observed implementation and evidence, with unknown format details left explicit.

validation: Use the accepted original browser build and compatible player-local input for an end-to-end fresh-browser import-to-launch scenario.
Observe unsupported/corrupt image, cancellation, clear/reimport, storage denial or eviction, and close/reopen save-reload outcomes.
Inspect the complete content path and network requests to confirm original files, converted assets, RAM, and saves remain local.
outOfScope: Declaring the complete minigame catalog or original offline behavior accepted; that evidence belongs to m2-verify.
Adding native helpers, remote conversion, uploads, peer transfer, telemetry attachments, or cloud synchronization of original content/state.
Inventing save formats, conversion support, browser budgets, or original gameplay behavior without evidence.
brief.stopCondition: Stop at unsupported image/build formats, unbounded memory or storage behavior, missing original-runtime capability, or any path that would transfer original content or state off-device; record the limit and do not substitute prototype rules or scenes.

references.purpose: Existing browser-local disc-session fixture and lifecycle calls.
Bounded local disc reader API and current session constraints.
Existing local asset conversion worker and no-return-of-original-file boundary.
Player-local content, storage, clear, and reimport constraints.

tasks.title: Accept the complete original offline inventory
tasks.scope: Build and execute the matching-build catalog/mode/reference matrix for the complete original offline game.

criteria.text: Every required game/variant, mode, character and arena is accounted for and exercised; all one-to-four-seat and original CPU cases are covered.
Original rules/presentation, save and full tournament scenarios pass; no required item is accepted as unknown, not reached or approximate.

brief.context: Produce evidence for the unchanged M2 complete-offline-game criteria against a verified original build. The public catalog leads and independent Twisted System prototype do not establish original inventory or parity; every required scope must have an evidence-backed disposition.
brief.firstStep: Bind the exact original build and matching browser/runtime identities, then derive a catalog and scenario matrix only from retained original-reference evidence, marking unresolved entries as blockers before execution.
prerequisites: M1 original browser execution is accepted.
m2-build fresh-browser conversion and local save/reload path is implemented for the declared supported build.
Matching-build original-reference scenarios and evidence access are available; gaps remain explicit.

deliverables.title: Build the evidence-backed catalog and variant inventory
deliverables.doneWhen: Every shipped selectable minigame and variant, character, arena, mode, and progression scope has an identified source/build and an explicit tested, unsupported, or unresolved disposition; no unresolved entry is counted as complete.

deliverables.title: Cover local seat counts and original CPU behavior
deliverables.doneWhen: Matching-build scenarios exercise one through four local seats and each required original CPU/difficulty case; the scenario record captures setup, inputs, outcomes, and any unavailable case.

deliverables.title: Exercise practice, Minigame Frenzy, and Tournament progression
deliverables.doneWhen: Original-reference scenarios cover practice, Minigame Frenzy, and full Tournament progression including round transitions and results for every required catalog entry, with unknown or untested paths listed as blockers.

deliverables.title: Complete the rules and presentation parity matrix
deliverables.doneWhen: Evidence-backed comparisons cover scoring and ties, rules, timing, movement and collisions, AI, camera, animation, audio, and progression for each required scenario; each discrepancy is recorded with severity, reproduction conditions, and disposition.

deliverables.title: Verify original save and tournament recovery cases
deliverables.doneWhen: Matching-build scenarios verify save/reload after browser close and reopen plus complete tournament checkpoint/recovery behavior; state and results match the recorded reference, while original-containing saves remain local.

deliverables.title: Publish the curated parity evidence and limits record
deliverables.doneWhen: A reviewable matrix links each required catalog/mode scenario to source/build identity, browser/device, observed outcome, evidence identity, discrepancy, and remaining limit; private media, raw reports, and proprietary data remain local.

validation: Compare each required scenario against the same identified original build and retain the recorded input/capture conditions.
Check every inventory row and parity dimension for explicit evidence-backed status; unknown, not reached, or approximate is a blocker.
Repeat the full save/reload and tournament scenarios after browser close/reopen and reconcile results against the reference record.
outOfScope: Treating static analysis, public footage, synthetic fixtures, standalone components, or Twisted System behavior as proof of original parity.
Filling catalog, mechanics, timing, asset, or save-format gaps with inferred behavior.
Adding online multiplayer, social services, mobile claims, or release acceptance.
brief.stopCondition: Do not accept or mark a required catalog entry or criterion complete while matching-build reference evidence is missing, the original behavior is unknown, or a discrepancy remains unresolved; preserve the explicit blocker and evidence boundary.

references.purpose: Authoritative M2 acceptance criteria, stable task identities, and dependencies.
Required original inventory, fidelity, and evidence standard.
Local content and save-state restrictions for verification.
Current prototype flow boundary; its rules and UI are not original-game proof.

milestones.title: Online multiplayer and recovery
milestones.foundation: Authority, content locality and four-seat ownership requirements are recorded; online services are unimplemented.
milestones.goal: The original game supports authoritative remote and mixed local/remote matches with recoverable tournament results.

criteria.text: Review and implement the execution/authority/content contract: the server owns outcomes, four total seats have explicit ownership, and original code/assets/RAM/save states remain local. Client-selected winners or a relay-only authority claim fail acceptance.

Pass four-browser and two-local-plus-two-remote cases across the required online catalog. Verify ten consecutive rounds per timing/contact/steering/orb family at 150 ms RTT, 30 ms jitter and 1% loss; music/pattern activities also pass an explicit audio/input fairness case.

Demonstrate disconnect/refresh/reconnect, stale-input handling, lobby-owner transfer and separate match-process recovery. Persist atomic tournament checkpoints/results, restore the committed state and prevent duplicate awards or seat ownership.

tasks.title: Implement authoritative mixed-seat match services
tasks.scope: Resolve the original-runtime/server contract and implement four-seat authority with local-content-safe messages and atomic results.

criteria.text: The reviewed protocol defines authority, identities, compatibility and required state without proprietary data transfer.
Server-owned outcomes, explicit seat ownership and atomic/idempotent tournament result writes are implemented and tested.

brief.context: Online authority remains unresolved and online services are unimplemented. The requirements must hold together: server-owned outcomes, original code/assets/RAM/saves local, and four total seats with explicit ownership. The current evidence does not prove a feasible authority route; the first work is a bounded source-only feasibility experiment and decision record. Match implementation is conditional on that decision.
brief.firstStep: Run the bounded authority feasibility spike before any match-service implementation: choose one narrowly named original scenario, inventory evidenced inputs/rules/outcomes and unknowns, define pass/fail independently for authority, locality, and recovery, and record whether the current contract is feasible, infeasible, or unresolved.
prerequisites: M2 is accepted, including the compatible original build and the verified offline scenarios needed to ground any online experiment.
The source-only feasibility spike has a reviewed decision; no accounts, lobbies, or netcode begin while authority is unresolved.
Any approved proposal preserves original code, assets, RAM, and original-containing saves locally and models four total seats.

deliverables.title: Determine whether server-owned outcomes can satisfy the local-content contract
deliverables.doneWhen: A bounded scenario record inventories only evidence-backed rules, inputs, timing, randomness, and outcomes, marks unknowns, specifies independent authority/locality/recovery pass-fail results, and records a reviewed feasible, infeasible, or unresolved decision without adding a server or sending original content/state.

deliverables.title: Specify a reviewed privacy-safe protocol envelope if feasible
deliverables.doneWhen: Only after a feasible authority decision, a reviewed protocol defines distinct account, connection, local profile, and seat identities; compatibility/version claims; bounded input ordering and stale/duplicate behavior; and explicit exclusion of assets, generated code, RAM, original-containing saves, and title-state blobs.

deliverables.title: Define ownership for four total local and remote seats
deliverables.doneWhen: The approved design documents and enforces exactly four total seats across local and remote owners, including mixed parties, and keeps account, connection, profile, and seat transfer rules distinct and reviewable.

deliverables.title: Implement only the authority route proven by the decision
deliverables.doneWhen: If and only if the feasibility decision supports implementation, server decisions for the declared supported scenarios are derived from the reviewed evidence-backed authority model and independently agree with original-reference outcomes; client-declared winners and relay-only sequencing cannot determine accepted results.

deliverables.title: Implement atomic tournament results and distinct recovery boundaries
deliverables.doneWhen: For the approved authority model, tournament checkpoints/results persist atomically and idempotently, and reconnect, lobby-owner transfer, and match-process recovery each have separate policies and observed outcomes without storing original-containing state remotely.

validation: Review the feasibility record for fixed scenarios, evidenced inputs/outcomes, explicit unknowns, and separate authority, locality, and recovery decisions before implementation work proceeds.

Demonstrate protocol and service messages contain no original assets/code, RAM, original-containing save states, or title-state blobs; a digest or signature is not treated as authority or access rights.
Exercise four-seat ownership, result idempotency, reconnect, lobby ownership transfer, and match-process recovery as separate cases against the reviewed decision.
outOfScope: Starting accounts, lobbies, or netcode while feasibility remains unresolved or fails under the current contract.
Running original title code, assets, RAM, or original-containing saves on a server or transferring them between peers.
Treating input sequencing, signatures, shared code, fixed ticks, client consensus, or relay as proof of server-owned outcomes.
brief.stopCondition: If authority cannot be demonstrated from evidence-backed outcomes while all original content/state stays local, stop before match implementation; record infeasible or unresolved status and required new evidence/options. Do not relax locality, claim relay authority, or invent rules to unblock implementation.

references.purpose: Unresolved decision, candidate routes, required bounded spike, privacy envelope, and separate recovery definitions.
Implemented source boundaries and product architecture contracts.
Original code/assets/RAM/save locality contract.
M3 acceptance criteria, stable task identities, and dependency order.

tasks.title: Verify online agreement, fairness and recovery
tasks.scope: Exercise remote/mixed parties, every required online catalog entry, impaired networks and recovery boundaries.

criteria.text: Remote and mixed-seat results agree under the defined network/fairness scenarios and representative repeated rounds.
Reconnect, ownership transfer and process recovery restore correct committed state without stuck inputs, duplicate rewards or leaked original content.

brief.context: M3 verification is conditional on an implemented authority route that has already passed its feasibility gate. It must evaluate the unchanged remote/mixed-seat, required-catalog network, fairness, and recovery criteria. If the route remains unresolved or fails, verification records the blocker without implying online capability.
brief.firstStep: Bind the reviewed authority decision, protocol/rules version, original build, runtime/converter identity, and candidate service build; translate the unchanged M3 criteria into a scenario matrix before running trials.
prerequisites: M2 offline game and original-reference scenario inventory are accepted.
m3-build authority feasibility decision is feasible and reviewed; unresolved or failed routes block match trials.
m3-build service, explicit four-seat ownership, and atomic results/recovery behavior are implemented for the declared scope.

deliverables.title: Verify remote and mixed four-seat party outcomes
deliverables.doneWhen: Four-browser remote and two-local-plus-two-remote scenarios run across the required online catalog; seat ownership and each accepted outcome are recorded against the server decision and the corresponding original-reference scenario.

deliverables.title: Exercise specified network impairment and repeated rounds
deliverables.doneWhen: Each required timing, contact, steering, and orb family completes ten consecutive rounds at 150 ms RTT, 30 ms jitter, and 1% loss with recorded conditions and outcomes; music/pattern activities also pass the explicit audio/input fairness case.

deliverables.title: Verify stale, late, duplicate, and disconnected input handling
deliverables.doneWhen: Defined stale-input, gap, duplicate, disconnect, refresh, and reconnect cases produce the reviewed protocol outcomes with no stuck inputs or unauthorized seat ownership, and no client-declared result is accepted.

deliverables.title: Verify lobby transfer and match-process recovery separately
deliverables.doneWhen: Lobby-owner transfer and interrupted match-process recovery are independently exercised; atomic checkpoint/result restoration preserves committed state and prevents duplicate awards, while reconnect alone is not counted as process recovery.

deliverables.title: Audit online traffic and durable storage for content locality
deliverables.doneWhen: Observed network payloads, service logs/diagnostics, checkpoints, and persisted results contain only reviewed protocol data and no original assets/code, RAM, original-containing saves, or derived proprietary content.

deliverables.title: Record matching-build online authority and recovery evidence
deliverables.doneWhen: A curated report binds source/service/protocol/rules identities, party and impairment scenarios, evidence identities, discrepancies, authority decision, and remaining limits; no scenario with missing or approximate outcomes is accepted.

validation: Run the exact four-browser and two-local-plus-two-remote cases over the required catalog and preserve the network profile for each run.
Check ten-round consecutive results per required family at the specified impairment values and record the audio/input fairness outcome.
Inspect recovery and locality evidence independently: reconnect, owner transfer, process restoration, atomic result writes, and excluded content payloads each receive their own disposition.
outOfScope: Verifying or advertising online multiplayer before a reviewed feasible authority decision and an implemented service exist.
Using client consensus or relayed inputs as a substitute for server-owned outcome evidence.
Changing the four-seat limit, required impairment profile, original-locality contract, or M3 acceptance criteria.
brief.stopCondition: Stop and record a failed or blocked scenario when the authority route is unresolved, original-reference agreement is missing, excluded content leaves the device, seat ownership exceeds four, or recovery duplicates/loses committed results; do not infer acceptance from protocol connectivity alone.

references.purpose: Unchanged M3 verification criteria and dependency on M2 and implementation.
Authority standard, locality exclusions, protocol boundaries, and separate recovery meanings.
Original behavior evidence and fidelity criteria for outcome comparison.
Four-seat, ownership, persistence, and server-authority contracts.

milestones.title: Player experience
milestones.foundation: Control Room Windows launcher, native F1 settings and three local UI replacements are implemented. Browser settings, accounts, friends and lobbies remain unfinished.
milestones.goal: Players can set up their content and controls, find friends, join lobbies and play/rematch through the supported browser interface.

criteria.text: Demonstrate fresh-account/recovery → content readiness → friend request/invite → public/private lobby or join code → ready/start → match → rematch. Verify permissions, privacy/block/report, incompatible content and rejected unauthorized API operations.

Verify per-seat keyboard/gamepad ownership, remapping/conflicts, calibration/prompts and saved preferences on named physical devices. Focus loss, disconnect/reconnect and stale input must produce the defined offline/online behavior without stuck actions.

Exercise keyboard-accessible navigation, visible focus, audio/fullscreen failure handling and quality/accessibility settings. Desktop support comes first; later mobile/touch support must pass these input flows and the M5 device matrix before it is advertised.

tasks.title: Complete accounts, friends and lobby flows
tasks.scope: Deliver account recovery, social permissions, content readiness and complete lobby/invite/rematch flows over the proven match service.

criteria.text: A fresh player can complete the account → friend/invite → compatible lobby → match/rematch journey.
Privacy, block/report, incompatible versions/content and unauthorized operations behave correctly.

brief.context: Control Room Windows launcher, native F1 settings and three local UI replacements are implemented. Browser settings, accounts, friends and lobbies remain unfinished. Native UI work supports reuse but does not implement the browser or online player journey.
brief.firstStep: Confirm the accepted M2/M3 evidence and the reviewed authority/content and identity boundaries before selecting service interfaces. Record any unresolved feasibility or policy decision as a blocker instead of inventing a client-authoritative match flow.
prerequisites: Full original content/journey integration requires accepted M2 conversion, compatible-content readiness and local-content behavior. Bounded UX and authorization design may proceed earlier when assigned.
Full online journey acceptance requires accepted M3 authority, four-seat ownership and recovery behavior. Source-owned interface work may proceed earlier without claiming working services.
An approved account/recovery, privacy, friend/invitation, and lobby authorization design with no proprietary content or original-containing state sent to services.

deliverables.title: Implement account creation, sign-in, and recovery journey
deliverables.doneWhen: A fresh browser can create or access an account, complete the approved recovery flow, and receive clear success, cancellation, and rejected-credential outcomes; tests show account identity remains distinct from connection, local profile, and seat identity.

deliverables.title: Implement friend requests and social privacy controls
deliverables.doneWhen: Two test accounts can request, accept, decline, and remove a friend relationship; privacy, block, and report actions have explicit authorized outcomes, and unauthorized API operations are rejected and covered by tests.

deliverables.title: Implement public/private lobby and invite readiness flows
deliverables.doneWhen: Authorized test players can create/join a public or private lobby or use a join code/invitation, and the service rejects incompatible content/runtime/rules readiness before start without transferring game files or derived title data.

deliverables.title: Enforce lobby seat ownership and four-seat limit
deliverables.doneWhen: Service checks demonstrate that a browser may own multiple local seats, remote seats have explicit owners, the combined lobby never exceeds four seats, and duplicate or unauthorized seat claims fail without changing the committed roster.

deliverables.title: Connect ready, start, match return, and rematch flows
deliverables.doneWhen: The supported interface completes content readiness → ready/start → the accepted match service → return/rematch for compatible test accounts, while refusal, disconnect, and failed-start states provide a recoverable user-visible result.

validation: Exercise a fresh-account/recovery-to-friend/invite-to-compatible-lobby-to-match/rematch scenario with at least two browser accounts and retain build and environment identity.
Test privacy/block/report, incompatible content or versions, forged or unauthorized API requests, duplicate seat claims, and the four-total-seat boundary.

Inspect protocol and diagnostics fixtures to confirm they carry only reviewed identifiers and gameplay protocol data, never original files, assets, generated title code, RAM, saves, or content-bearing attachments.
outOfScope: Changing original-game rules, claiming client relays are authoritative, or weakening the M3 content-locality or four-seat contract.
Xbox Live integration, voice/free-form chat, spectators, larger parties, ranked play, and mobile/touch support.
Selecting a production vendor, granting legal/licensing rights, authorizing service spend, or publishing/deploying a service.
brief.stopCondition: Stop before implementation if M2/M3 are not accepted or the authority/content, identity, privacy, or authorization contract is unresolved; during work stop at any path that requires proprietary content/state transfer or an unreviewed authority assumption.

references.purpose: Unresolved authority/content feasibility boundary and candidate protocol envelope.
Current absence of production online services and required identity, seat, and recovery distinctions.
Player-local content and data-transfer constraints for accounts, compatibility, and online flows.
Canonical M4/M3 criteria and unchanged milestone/work-package dependency identities.

tasks.title: Accept owned controls and browser usability
tasks.scope: Complete and exercise controls/preferences, focus/device lifecycle and accessible browser navigation with physical devices.

criteria.text: Keyboard/gamepad remapping, conflicts, calibration/prompts and multiple owned seats work without stuck or misrouted input.
Named device/browser sessions verify preferences, focus/disconnect, navigation, audio/fullscreen and quality settings; touch/mobile claims require their own observed cases.

brief.context: The existing research app provides configurable local keyboard/gamepad ownership and focus/disconnect clearing for a prototype. That is not evidence for physical-device behavior in the supported product or for production accounts/lobbies; M4 verification must bind observations to the tested build, browser, and devices.
brief.firstStep: Freeze the candidate build and write a device/browser scenario matrix naming each physical keyboard/gamepad, seat assignment, remap, lifecycle event, accessibility path, and expected result before collecting acceptance evidence.
prerequisites: M4 build flows are available on a candidate that has passed the issue's targeted checks; preserve the M4 build dependency.
M2 and M3 accepted build/evidence identities are available for content readiness, online ownership, and recovery behavior.
Named physical test devices and desktop browsers are available; report unavailable hardware/cases as unverified rather than inferred.

deliverables.title: Verify local seat and physical-device ownership
deliverables.doneWhen: For one through four total seats, the retained matrix records which physical keyboard/gamepad owns each seat, proves each action reaches only its assigned seat, and distinguishes multiple local seats from remote seats and account/connection/profile identities.

deliverables.title: Verify remapping, conflicts, calibration, and prompts
deliverables.doneWhen: Named-device runs cover keyboard/gamepad remapping, duplicate/conflicting assignments, calibration and player prompts; each accepted or rejected change has an observed result and no input is routed to another seat.

deliverables.title: Verify focus loss and controller lifecycle recovery
deliverables.doneWhen: On each declared physical gamepad/browser combination, focus loss, tab hiding, disconnect, reconnect, reassignment, stale input, and resume are exercised with no stuck action; the observed offline/online behavior matches the reviewed contract.

deliverables.title: Verify keyboard navigation and visible focus
deliverables.doneWhen: A keyboard-only run reaches and operates account/setup, lobby, match, settings, error, and recovery controls in a meaningful order, with visible focus and no keyboard trap; deviations are recorded against the candidate build.

deliverables.title: Verify audio/fullscreen failures and user settings
deliverables.doneWhen: Named desktop browser runs exercise denied/unavailable audio and fullscreen behavior plus quality/accessibility preferences, recording clear failure handling and whether preferences survive the supported session lifecycle.

validation: Retain a reproducible matrix with source/build identity, browser/OS version, physical device identifiers, seat ownership, steps, expected/observed outcome, and evidence links for every declared case.
Tie the end-to-end fresh-account/recovery → content readiness → friend/invite → lobby → ready/start → match → rematch evidence to the same supported build and accepted M2/M3 boundaries.
Classify absent devices, unsupported browsers, touch/mobile, and unrun scenarios as limits; do not infer physical-device support from mocks or component fixtures.
outOfScope: Changing acceptance criteria or creating extra native issues for each device, browser, or matrix row.
Claiming mobile/touch support without its own observed input flows and M5 device-matrix evidence.
Treating synthetic gamepad/controller fixtures or the independent prototype as original-game or production-service acceptance.
brief.stopCondition: Stop and leave the affected case open when a named physical-device outcome, account/lobby flow, or expected offline/online failure behavior cannot be observed or is inconsistent; do not substitute synthetic evidence or broaden the advertised support matrix.

references.purpose: Existing local seat ownership, assignment conflict, and input-clearing behavior to target with real-device checks.
Existing focus, visibility, and disconnect event handling under verification.
Current research-app keyboard/gamepad behavior and limits of public checks.
Canonical M4 acceptance requirements, including physical-device and browser usability cases.

milestones.title: Release readiness
milestones.foundation: Published browser and Windows preview packages, pinned builds, source-only publication guards and Windows/Linux CI.
milestones.goal: Ship a reproducible, documented and operationally supported release for the declared browser/device matrix.

criteria.text: Accept M1–M4 and reproduce the candidate from a clean checkout using pinned inputs/tool versions. Required CI and publication checks pass; distributed source/builds and diagnostics contain no original media, generated title code or credentials.

Freeze and test the required desktop Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Safari and named hardware matrix. Record full-tournament soak/relaunch/save/recovery, frame times toward 60 fps with a usable documented 30 fps mode, peak memory, import time and failure behavior against budgets fixed before acceptance runs.

Verify protocol/content/rules/converter versioning, deployment/rollback, backup/restore, capacity/admission limits, privacy/data handling and release documentation. Resolve licensing/content-release questions and authorize service costs/deployment before publication; later mobile releases pass the same applicable gates.

tasks.title: Verify reproducible source-only release operations
tasks.scope: Prepare the release candidate, version compatibility, operational recovery and documented deployment/cost/licensing decisions.

criteria.text: A clean checkout produces the candidate and passes source/CI checks without proprietary content or credentials in artifacts.
Versioning, rollback, backup/restore, capacity/privacy and release/cost decisions have reviewable procedures and evidence.

brief.context: Pinned Node/npm inputs, source-only build guards, and Windows/Linux CI exist, but the candidate is not yet a reproducible accepted release and production operations are not authorized by the backlog. The release package must remain clean and source-only; licensing, service cost, and deployment require separate explicit decisions.
brief.firstStep: Inventory the pinned toolchain, required CI/publication checks, existing clean-build steps, and release decision owners; define a candidate manifest and artifact allowlist before preparing release procedures.
prerequisites: M1 through M4 acceptance records and matching source/build identities are available before release readiness is claimed.
Pinned source/tool inputs and required CI/publication checks are recorded, with a clean checkout available for reproduction.
Named owners and decision records exist for licensing/content release, privacy/data handling, deployment, and any service costs; unresolved authorization remains a release blocker.

deliverables.title: Reproduce the candidate from a clean pinned checkout
deliverables.doneWhen: A documented clean-checkout procedure uses the pinned Node/npm and declared source/tool inputs to reproduce the candidate and records commit, commands, tool versions, output identities, and any nondeterminism.

deliverables.title: Verify source-only artifact and diagnostic allowlists
deliverables.doneWhen: Candidate source/build/diagnostic paths are checked against an explicit allowlist and scan evidence shows no original media, generated title code, original-containing state, credentials, or unapproved private artifacts are distributed or attached.

deliverables.title: Document protocol and content compatibility versioning
deliverables.doneWhen: A reviewed compatibility table identifies protocol, rules, converter/runtime, and content-build identifiers, supported combinations, and explicit mismatch rejection behavior without implying that an identifier proves possession or authority.

deliverables.title: Prepare rollback, backup, recovery, and capacity procedures
deliverables.doneWhen: Reviewable runbooks define candidate rollback, backup/restore checks, admission/capacity limits, privacy/data handling, and operational evidence owners, while clearly marking any unimplemented or unapproved production service step.

deliverables.title: Record licensing, deployment, and cost decisions for review
deliverables.doneWhen: A decision register names the licensing/content-release questions, deployment target, estimated service costs, approver, and authorization state; unresolved or unauthorized items remain explicit blockers and no publication or spend is triggered by this issue.

validation: Run the declared clean-checkout reproduction and required CI/publication checks, retaining commit, tool versions, logs/receipts, and artifact hashes without private or credential-bearing data.
Inspect exact candidate and diagnostic paths against source-only policy; report excluded private inputs separately from public-check results.
Review version mismatch, rollback, restore, capacity/admission, and privacy procedures through source-owned fixtures or documented dry runs; label dry-run evidence accurately.
outOfScope: Publishing a release/site, deploying production services, purchasing capacity, or authorizing service spend.
Selecting or asserting a repository/content license or legal permission without the responsible explicit decision.
Automatically adding mobile/touch, expanded browser support, or new feature scope to the release candidate.
brief.stopCondition: Stop release promotion if any M1–M4 gate is unaccepted, clean reproduction or source-only checks fail, operational recovery/privacy controls are unverified, or required licensing/deployment/cost authorization is unresolved; keep the reviewable candidate and blocker record without publishing or spending.

references.purpose: Pinned Node/npm requirements and source-owned check/build command inventory.
Required Windows/Linux continuous-integration checks and runner coverage.
Source-only publication, local-content, diagnostics, and privacy boundaries.
Milestone acceptance evidence and distinction between reviewed scope, native tracking, and publication.

tasks.title: Accept browser/device performance and release evidence
tasks.scope: Run the frozen browser/hardware matrix and full-product soak, import, input and recovery scenarios.

criteria.text: Required desktop browsers and named hardware pass the agreed frame/memory/import budgets, full-tournament sessions and recovery cases.
All milestone acceptance records and remaining supported-device limits are reviewed; no unsupported platform or unfinished feature is advertised.

brief.context: M5 requires actual browser/device and full-product evidence against budgets fixed before the runs. Existing source checks and prototype fixtures do not establish title performance, complete browser support, or release readiness; the candidate must inherit accepted M1–M4 evidence and preserve its limits.
brief.firstStep: Freeze the candidate source/build identities, declare required desktop browser versions and named hardware, then set frame-time, memory, import-time, and recovery budgets with rationale before any acceptance run starts.
prerequisites: M1, M2, M3, and M4 acceptance records are reviewed for the same declared product candidate and supported scope.
M5 build candidate has a reproducible clean-checkout record and required source/CI/publication checks pass.
Browser/device matrix, measurable budgets, scenario procedures, and evidence-retention plan are frozen before testing; no target is selected after observing results.

deliverables.title: Execute the declared desktop browser and hardware matrix
deliverables.doneWhen: Each required Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari version and named hardware configuration has a candidate-bound result for the declared launch, content, input, and recovery scenarios; unsupported or unavailable combinations are listed as limits.

deliverables.title: Measure frame time, memory, and import budgets
deliverables.doneWhen: Every matrix run reports measured frame-time distribution against the predeclared 60 fps target and usable documented 30 fps mode, peak memory, import time, and failure behavior against the budgets frozen before runs.

deliverables.title: Verify full-tournament soak and relaunch recovery
deliverables.doneWhen: The declared long-session scenarios complete a full tournament and exercise relaunch, save/reload, recovery, and failure injection on named devices, with captured outcomes and all discrepancies linked to the candidate identity.

deliverables.title: Review release evidence, procedures, and supported-scope claims
deliverables.doneWhen: A reviewer can trace every M1–M5 acceptance record, compatibility/version procedure, rollback/restore/privacy evidence, and authorized release decision; release documentation lists only observed supported browsers/devices and unresolved limits.

deliverables.title: Record pass, fail, or blocked disposition
deliverables.doneWhen: The evidence record gives a criterion-by-criterion pass/fail/blocked disposition tied to one source commit, candidate, browser/device matrix, and reviewer; no missing result is silently treated as a pass.

validation: Confirm budget values and matrix identifiers were committed/frozen before each run and preserve raw measurements locally with curated non-content result identities.
Repeat required soak/recovery cases on the declared supported matrix and bind logs, build hashes, device/browser details, and failures to the same candidate.
Audit every advertised browser/device and release claim against completed observations; later mobile/touch remains outside the declared release unless it passes applicable input and release gates.
outOfScope: Inventing performance budgets after runs, treating 128 MiB/120-second importer proposals as measured guarantees, or inferring title performance from fixtures.
Adding later mobile/touch support automatically or accepting untested browser/hardware combinations by similarity.
Approving licensing, deployment, or costs on behalf of the owner, publishing a site, or releasing proprietary/derived game material.
brief.stopCondition: Stop acceptance and mark the affected criterion failed or blocked when frozen budgets, browser/device cases, soak/recovery evidence, milestone records, or required owner authorizations are missing or fail; do not advertise or publish an unsupported release.

references.purpose: M5 acceptance gates, inherited M1–M4 evidence requirement, and later-device release boundary.
Browser/device performance evidence and requirement to freeze budgets before acceptance runs.
Current gaps in browser performance, reproducibility, privacy, licensing, and operating cost evidence.
Canonical M5 criteria and unchanged work-package acceptance dependencies.
